::: {.notice}
**Evidence type.** The results in this project come from **simulations** of a multi-PMT optical module. They have not yet been demonstrated on deployed detector hardware.
:::

## Scientific motivation

Large neutrino observatories lose detection efficiency to **deadtime**: periods when a sensor channel cannot record light because of photomultiplier saturation, digitizer limits or front-end readout constraints. Conventional coincidence triggers implicitly assume that every sensor is always available, so their efficiency drops when channels go temporarily offline.

## Objectives

- Formulate a trigger observable that degrades gracefully, instead of collapsing, when channels are not live.
- Keep the design suitable for low-latency implementation on FPGA-based front-end electronics.
- Quantify event recovery against conventional coincidence logic under increasing deadtime.

## Methodology

The approach separates two stages:

1. **Continuous measurement construction.** At each sensor node a recursive (IIR) update builds a continuity-preserving observable that decays smoothly during non-live periods.
2. **Discrete trigger decision.** The trigger acts on these observables rather than on raw hit coincidences, so a temporarily dead channel reduces, but does not erase, its contribution.

A companion study tests geometric scoring of the recursive state across the PMTs of a multi-PMT module, and a related preprint develops time-aligned coherence estimation for multichannel data with intermittent observations.

## Simulation framework

Studies use a simulated multi-PMT optical module for neutrino telescopes with configurable channel deadtime.

<!-- OWNER TO ADD: simulation tool chain (e.g. language, photon/PMT response model, deadtime model) and one figure of trigger efficiency vs deadtime probability, with alt text. -->

## Key results and limitations

In simulation, the liveness-aware trigger recovered more events than conventional coincidence logic when the probability of channel deadtime was high (see the CHEP 2026 contributions and arXiv:2601.18114). Results are limited to simulated detector conditions; hardware validation and comparison against real detector deadtime data remain future work.
